la:adj:prorsus.html:
prorsus (collat. form prōsus; v. II.), a, um, adj.
for pro-versus
.
Straightforwards, right onwards, straight, direct (post-Aug.): prorso tramite siste gradus (al. proso),: prorsi limites appellantur in agrorum mensuris, qui ad orientem directi sunt,, and Paul. ex Müll.—
Trop., of style, straightforwards, i. e. prosaic, in prose, opp. to verse (post-class.): prorsum est porro versum, id est ante versum. Hinc et prorsa oratio, quam non inflexit cantilena, Don. : et prorsa et vorsa facundia veneratus sum,in prose and verse,.—In this sense predominant (but not found in Cic.) in the form prosa oratio, prose, =soluta oratio, ; : prosa eloquentia,; Sen. ap. ; ; .—Subst.: prōsa, ae, f., prose, ; ; ; 9, 4, 52 et saep.

la:adv:prorsus.html:
prorsus (collat. form prōsus, ; Enn. ap. ; Trag. Rel. p. 28 Rib.; but p. 107 Vahl. reads prorsus), adv.
for pro-versus
.
Forwards (ante-class.): non prorsus, verum transvorsus cedit, quasi cancer solet,.—
Straight on, right onwards, directly (ante- and post-class.), Cato ap. Müll.: tunc Arionem prorsus ex eo loco Corinthum petivisse,.—
Trop.
Straightway, by all means, certainly, truly, precisely, utterly, absolutely (class.): prorsus perii,: vide ne ille huc prorsus se inruat,; : prorsus tacere nequeo,: ita

prorsus existimo, : nullo modo potest fleri prosus,: nullo modo prorsus assentior,; : verbum prorsus nullum intellego,not a single word,: venies exspectatus non solum nobis, sed prorsus omnibus,: affatim prorsus,: prorsus vehementer et severe,: hoc mihi prorsus valde placet,; .—Ironically: grati prorsus conjugibus revertemur,.—

Exactly, just, precisely: set ea prorsus opportuna Catilinae,; dub.; v. Müll. ad h. l.: prorsus quasi,precisely as if,.—
After an enumeration of particulars, in short, in fine, in a word: igitur colos exsanguis, foedi oculi: citus modo, modo tardus incessus; prorsus in facie vultuque vecordia inerat,; ; ;

la:verb:prorogo.gloss: to prolong, draw out, keep (something) going
senses: to prolong, draw out, keep (something) going
to extend (a term of office, a certain situation)
to preserve, keep for a long time, continue
to pay down beforehand, advance money from one account to another
la:verb:prorogo.html:
prō-rŏgo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
To prolong, continue, extend, protract (class.; syn.: propago, produco): ne quinquennii imperium Caesari prorogaretur,should not be prolonged,: provinciam,; : ne quid temporis nobis prorogetur (in the province),: imperium,: imperium in insequentem annum,; : spatium praeturae in alterum annum,: spem militi in alium diem,: vitae spatium,: moras in hiemes,: memoriam alicujus,: nominis famam,.—
Transf.
To keep for a long time, to preserve, continue (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): divinis condimentis utere, quī prorogare vitam possis hominibus,: alterum in lustrum, meliusque semper Proroget aevum,: spiritum homini,; : conditum prorogatur,.—
To put off, defer (class.): dies ad solvendum,: diem mortis,.—
To pay down beforehand, to advance (post-class.): vel prorogante eo, vel repromittente,: si ei nummos prorogavit emptor,: pensionem integram,.—
To propagate, perpetuale (post-class.): prorogata familia,: sobolem, (dub.; al. generandam).

la:noun:prorogatio.html:
prōrŏgātĭo, ōnis, f.
prorogo
.
A prolonging, extension of a term of office: prorogatio imperii,a prolongation of one's command,—
A putting off, deferring of an appointed time: diei, (in , the true reading is perrogationem; in , propagatio).

la:noun:prora.html:
prōra, ae (collat. form prōris; acc. prorim, Att. ap. , or Trag. 575), f., = πρώρα.
The forepart of a ship, the prow (opp. puppis, the stern; class.): astitit prorae,; : prorae admodum erectae,: rostrata,: terris advertere proram,; ; : prorae tutela Melanthus, i. e. the lookout stationed at the prow, = proreta, : suspensa prora navim in puppim statuebat,: prorae litore illisae,; ; .—Prov.: mihi prora et puppis, ut Graecorum proverbium est, fuit a me tui dimittendi, ut rationes nostras explicares, i. e. my intention from beginning to end, my whole design, Gr. πρώρα καὶ πρύμνη, .—
Poet., transf., a ship: quot prius aeratae steterant ad litora prorae,; .

la:verb:prorumpo.gloss: to break or burst forth or out
senses: to break or burst forth or out
la:verb:prorumpo.html:
prō-rumpo, rūpi, ruptum, 3, v. a. and n.
Act., to thrust or cast forth, to cause to break, burst, or rush forth, to send forth: (Aetna) atram prorumpit ad aethera nubem,: proruptus pons,broken down, (al. proruto).—With se, to burst forth, dash forth: cerva in fugam sese prorupit,.—Mid.: prorumpi, to rush or burst forth: hinc prorumpitur in mare venti vis,: mare proruptum,: proruptum exundat pelagus,: proruptus corpore sudor,: prorupto sanguine,.—
Neutr., to rush or break forth, to burst out.
Lit.: per medios audacissime proruperunt,: in hostes,: obsessi omnibus portis prorumpunt,. —
Transf., of things, to break out, break or burst forth, make its appearance: cum diu cohibitae lacrimae prorumperent,: vis morbi in unum intestinum prorupit,: incendium proruperat,a fire had broken out,: stercora,: prorumpit in auras vox,: nihil prorupit, quo conjuratio intellegeretur,became known,.—
Trop., to break out, burst forth: illa pestis prorumpet,: eo prorumpere hominum cupiditatem, ut, etc.,: in bellum,to break out,: in scelera ac dedecora,: ad minas,to break out into threats,: ad quod victo silentio prorupit reus,at which he broke silence and burst forth,; 12, 54; 13, 12.
la:verb:prorumpo.inflection: rūpi, ruptum, 3, v. a. and n.

la:verb:proripio.html:
prō-rĭpĭo, pŭi, reptum, 3, v. a.
To drag or snatch forth (class.).
Lit.: hominem proripi jubet,: nudos pedes,i. e. spring forth,.—With se, to rush out, to hasten or hurry forth or away: quo illum hunc hominem proripuisse foras se dicam ex aedibus?: se ex curiā repente proripuit,: se ex curiā domum,: se porta foras, (12 init.); 1, 80: se domo,; : ex totā urbe,.—
Trop.: quae libido non se proripiet ac proiciet occultatione propositā?.—
To snatch or hurry on, forwards, or away.
Lit.: se in publicum,to rush into the street,; : se in silvam,to take refuge,: se custodibus,: se cursu,to run away,.—Without se (poet.): quo deinde ruis? quo proripis?.—
Trop. (poet.): ne virilis Cultus in caedem, et Lycias proriperet catervas?.

la:verb:proruo.html:
prō-rŭo, rŭi, rŭtum, 3, v. a. and n.
Act., to cast or tear down in front, to pull down, throw down, hurl to the ground, overthrow, overturn, demolish (class.): his (munitionibus) prorutis,: vallo proruto, jam in castra proclium intulerat,; ; columnam,: Albam a fundamentis,to raze to the ground,: vallum in fossas,; : terrae motus montes,: terrae motibus prorutae domus,thrown down,: prorutae arbores,: proruere ac profligare hostem,to overthrow,.—With se, to rush out, hurry forth (poet.): foras simul omnes proruunt se,: prorutus tumulo cinis,.—
Neutr.
To rush forth, to rush or fall upon an enemy: ex parte, quā (dextrum cornu) proruebat, : proruere in hostem,; cf. .—
To tumble down (post-Aug.): motu terrae oppidum proruit,.
la:verb:proruo.inflection: rŭi, rŭtum, 3, v. a. and n.
